To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose a novel model agnostics framework for explaining the behaviour of any black box model through the joint optimization of fidelity to the original classifier and interpretability of its explanations.

we propose a model-agnostic framework for producing interpretable explanations of black-box models, and we develop a novel optimization objective that enables us to produce accurate, interpretable, and user-interactive explanations of black-box predictive models.
BETA can generate compact, easy-to-interpret explanations for any black box model, and that users find BETA’s explanations more understandable and useful compared to baselines.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of providing explanations for the predictions of black-box models.
the problem of generating interpretable and explorable approximations of black-box models.
the problem of generating explanations of black box predictive models in an interactive manner.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

BETA is the first framework that is capable of generating global explanations of the behaviour of any black box model through simultaneous optimisation of interpretability, unambiguity and fidelity, while also allowing user interaction to explore the model based on their preferences.
we have developed a novel model agnostics framework for explaining the behaviour of any given black-box classifier by optimizing for fidelity to original model and interpretablity of the explanation.
we propose a novel framework for explaining the behaviour of any given black-box classifier by generating a small number of interpretable, compact and unambiguous decision sets.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

our approach provides a general and principled approach for producing global explanations of black-box models, and allows users to interactively and efficiently explore model behavior based upon their preferences.
we propose a novel model agnostics framework to explain the behavior of any classifier by simultaneously optimizing interpretability and fidelity to the original classifier.
we are proposing a new approach to explain any black-box model by learning interpretable and explorable decision sets.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in addition to the usual accuracy and interpretability requirements of an explanation method, the ability to interactively explore the model's behavior in the context of user preferences should be a key design consideration for explanation methods.
we show how to learn a small set of simple, yet powerful, decision sets that can explain the behavior of any arbitrary black box model.
it is possible to generate highly compact and accurate global approximations of any given black-box predictive model that can be easily interpreted by a human.
